tasks.title: Init and day-2 commands share lock, safe-write, spawn and readiness helpers
tasks.spec: ## Repository: deploy, Reuse (extract before the second use), shared files and Tool facts; Decisions 3, 4, 7-9 and 13; Security impact and Rollout order. FIRST extract the owned .pulse-init.lock and atomicWrite/link/mode checks from cli/write-install.ts into tested cli/lock.ts and cli/safe-write.ts; migrate init before adding consumers. Preserve lock nonce/ownership and recorded signals, change refusal to 'another pulse command is running in <dir> (or remove .pulse-init.lock if none is)', and fsync both file and containing directory. safe-write.ts owns the single validate-on-read/write-state-before-side-effect helper shared by rotation-journal and upgrade.json, durable rename and archive finalization. Put open/read/write/fsync/rename/unlink behind ONE injected file seam with named failure and hard-kill boundaries and recorded token-file reads. It must distinguish staging temp write, temp-file fsync, staging rename, its directory fsync, staged journal write, install rename, its directory fsync and saved journal write, including errors after a successful rename and the reconcile's own directory fsync. Test the file primitives here; keep journal reconciliation, credential read order and the complete rotation matrices in T4. Extend cli/docker.ts's only spawn seam for input, stdinFd and stdoutFd, preserving ignored stdin by default, bounded calls and Docker exit 3; distinguish missing binaries by name so missing gh can exit 1. Extend cli/ready.ts's parsePs with full ID and readyz/waitReady with container-id targeting rather than adding a poller. Implement constant API_SCRIPT (stdin JSON, fixed localhost URL, 10 s fetch timeout, redirect error, 1 MiB response cap), status parsing and the 10 s bounded timingSafeEqual file comparison in cli/api-call.ts. API_SCRIPT starts with // pulse-cli-api-call/1 and has an unref'd process.exit(70) timer at 11 s so an in-container call ends even if the docker exec client is killed. The same module owns constant SETTLE_SCRIPT: scan every other /proc/<pid>/cmdline for the API marker, assemble the marker from two string parts so the scanner does not contain it, and print the count without any bearer. Its injected-clock settle poll runs every 500 ms for at most 30 s; count 0 is settled, an exec failure or timeout exits 1. Test transport/scanner/poll mechanics here; the order of settle, create, sweeps and journal transitions belongs to T4. Return the already-parsed effective Compose model in Project from checkConfig/resolveProject, preserving its override and --no-interpolate guard call and requiring no second config call. Rotation reads locations and upgrade reads effective images and persistent mounts from this model with own()/isObj. Export/reuse own()/isObj from cli/docker.ts and assertPin/PULSE_IMAGE from cli/services.ts; services.ts and its tests are declared because Reuse explicitly requires them. Extend cli/test/fake-docker.ts as the only fake spawn, recording input, fds, signals, full container ids/states and a named stop-at-step hook for the rotation and upgrade matrices. Every shared module states what it owns and tests its variants; no duplicate guards, pin patterns, spawns, file seams, state writers or readiness loops. The same file seam must fail all four parts of an upgrade state write (temp write, temp fsync, rename, directory fsync), with the completed rename still observable when directory fsync fails. The state helper exposes a validated read-back after an error; consumers, not the primitive, choose rotation reconciliation or the Decision 13 action table. Keep those command-specific recovery decisions in T4/T5.

acceptance.expected: 0 failing tests; .pulse-init.lock refuses a second owner and never removes a changed owner's lock; init preserves valid tokens/keys and records interrupts; writes use wx, final mode, file fsync, rename and directory fsync, refusing links and unsafe modes. State readers reject malformed literal fixtures and an injected fsync failure prevents the next side effect. The one injected file seam records every token-file read and can stop at open/read/write/file-fsync/directory-fsync/rename/unlink boundaries with an ordinary error or a hard kill without cleanup. A successful rename followed by a directory-fsync error is observable on disk; the caller can reread the on-disk state instead of treating the thrown error as proof that the rename failed. Atomic rename preserves the old or new complete file. Absent input keeps stdin ignored, input closes stdin, fd streams preserve literal bytes, and full 64-hex ps IDs select the intended container. API transport uses stdin only with 10 s/1 MiB/redirect:error; equality prints only same or different. Docker ENOENT remains exit 3 and missing gh is distinguished by name. The exported PULSE_IMAGE and assertPin accept runtime-assembled valid pulse shapes and reject malformed shapes without a pin literal in tests. The sole fake spawn records options/signals and its named hook stops the selected step. Focused coverage is not the coverage gate. The four-part state-write seam supports both ordinary errors and hard kills, including a successful state rename followed by a failed directory fsync; the validated read-back returns the on-disk old/new state without retrying the write. Project exposes the literal effective model returned by the sole guarded resolution call, including override mounts/environment; 0 extra config calls. API_SCRIPT's literal first-line marker is pulse-cli-api-call/1, fetch timeout is 10000 ms and self-exit is code 70 within 11000 ms even after the exec client ends. SETTLE_SCRIPT excludes its own PID and does not contain the contiguous marker in its argv; fixtures with 2 marked clients and an unrelated process print 2, and with no marked clients print 0. Fake-clock settle polls at 500 ms, succeeds only on 0, and an exec failure or 30000 ms limit returns failure without a bearer or secret in argv/env/output.

tasks.spec: ## Repository: deploy, rotation-journal, token-rotate, command wiring, api-call consumer checks and docs; Decisions 1 and 3-9; Required behavior (token rotate and Help and docs); Counterexamples (Selection, Order, Handoff resume, Lost answer, Stage boundary, Reconcile bearer order, Revoke guard, Journal resume, 409, Legacy api, Files, No secret in argv); Acceptance evidence 1 (production behavior), 3 (rotation, stage-boundary, rotate-outcome and Delayed create matrices), 5-6; Security impact and Rollout order. Use cli/lock.ts, cli/safe-write.ts's shared state reader/writer and injected file seam, cli/api-call.ts, resolveProject/guarded, readyz/waitReady/parsePs, tokenContentValid, shown() and firstLine/maskUserInfo; extend the sole cli/test/fake-docker.ts helper. Keep the complete rotation state machine and its recovery matrices together. Preflight every location/candidate/file and exactly-one ready consumer before any POST; record full oldContainerId. Implement requested/replacing/staged/saved/refreshing/refreshed/handoff/switched/revoking/done with durable states, validation, activeTokenId/revokeTokenId/replacementName and old/new container IDs. Stage every rotate/create secret through a wx 0600 temp, file fsync, rename to secrets/.pulse-next.<file>.<id> and directory fsync; journal staged with activeTokenId BEFORE installing by rename over the host file, fsync the directory, then journal saved. On EVERY resume AND EVERY error anywhere in this stage/save sequence, discard the in-memory answer secret and execute Decision 8's reconcile immediately in the same process, rereading the journal from disk. Do not classify a stage error itself as a lost answer. Reconcile order is journal validation; recognized temp cleanup plus secrets-directory fsync; complete staging name/file/state/ownership matching without API calls; replacing-row read-only confirmation; then actions in journal order. If reconcile's cleanup fsync or a state/install write fails, exit 1 with the durable journal and staging files kept for a rerun, without retrying another row. No OWNED host token file may be read until reconcile finishes. For replacing admin, use the validated staging secret as bearer; for replacing probe, the independent secrets/admin-token is not owned by the journal and is the ONLY allowed host bearer during reconcile. Require one shared event log from the file seam and fake api, in this order: all staging checks; lstat of the independent admin file (regular, not a link, mode checked); its read and tokenContentValid; GET /admin/tokens/self with that content (200/admin); then GET /admin/tokens/<replacementId>. The capability call must follow the read, because it needs that bearer. Invalid staging refuses before even reading that admin file. Recover requested/replacing with a matching staged answer; distinguish staged-with-file from staged-without-file; refuse inconsistent/second staging files. A post-staging-rename directory-fsync error with the original token's staged secret follows requested -> staged -> saved, with no create or revoke. States never return to replacing after staged. Enter replacing or sweep exact-name orphans ONLY after reconcile found no staging file; no held secret is an orphan. Before EVERY revoke, GET self and refuse either the authenticating id or activeTokenId, keeping the journal. Use the SAME Decision 8 Rotate outcome table in the first run and resume: class ok is parsed 200; rejected is a complete JSON refusal with status 400/401/403/404/405/409/413/429; ambiguous covers timeout, transport error, 5xx, other status and malformed 200; none is resume. For every non-ok class, read back same/changed/gone/unknown. Only changed readback or an ok answer lost during staging after reconcile found no staging file permits replacing. Rejected+same/gone drops the item and later requested items, exits 1 with fixed status text, and never creates; ambiguous/none+same permits one normal retry; ambiguous/none+gone drops/exits; unknown exits with requested retained. At most 2 rotate POSTs per item per run, at most 1 applied rotation. A late first request can land before a retry 409; changed readback then uses replacement. Persist replacementName/revokeTokenId before create. Decision 8 Lost answer step 2 first settles every prior create with cli/api-call.ts's SETTLE_SCRIPT, then reads the token list and revokes every exact-name active orphan through the revoke guard. This runs only after reconcile found no staging file, so no replacement secret is held. Before ANY sweep list or later create, settle the preceding create, including one left in flight by a killed run. A failed settle exits 1 with the journal retained and sends no sweep/create. Classify create 201/rejected/ambiguous: parsed 201 stages/saves; a documented rejection exits 1 with no further create; an ambiguous response OR a create secret lost after stage-error reconciliation returns to settle then sweep before another create. At most 2 create POSTs per item/run. Before an attempted third, finish the second settle/sweep, then exit 1 in replacing with no in-flight create and no active unheld replacement. In switched, when replacementName is set, ALWAYS settle and perform the final exact-name sweep excluding activeTokenId, including on resume, before revoking the lost original token or deleting the journal. Print revoked <n> unheld replacement token(s) only when the final sweep revoked tokens. Failed final settle or unconfirmed revoke keeps switched for retry. Keep independent tokens with other names. The fake API can hold, apply or drop creates at named events and drives SETTLE_SCRIPT counts plus the injected clock; test all seven Acceptance 3 Delayed create cases for both kinds. Stage/save/switch a held replacement then revoke only the lost id. Use ONE fake API helper mapping secrets to ids and enforcing real revoked-secret 401, permitted self-revocation and last-admin 409. Probe handoff follows the observed-container resume table without rescaling old+new; new readiness, 10 s bounded same-token check and 2000 ms precede old stop/removal. Cover missing/stopped/duplicate/new-only containers and repeated different. Admin identity precedes console recreate/readiness/equality/own-file identity. Only necessary consumers change, locations run serially, and output reports inspect-derived W or unknown when old is gone. Record signals through API/staging/install/state/reconcile critical sections, the rotate outcome readback/retry, all create settling/sweeps (including the final sweep) and bounded second create, then exit 130 at the next boundary. Except for the explicit settle timeout, a signal never exits between an ambiguous create and its settle/sweep; a hard kill leaves journal-backed recovery. Parse selectors, journal-argument matching and timeout 1-3600 default 120; handle 401/403/404/409/429 and malformed replies safely. Wire HELP/COMMANDS/dispatch/errors. Add command and Token recovery docs including secret-bearing staging files (never delete manually during a journal), reconcile order and the independent admin-bearer exception, stage-error recovery, reconcile/revoke refusals, the Rotate outcome rows that drop items or retain the journal, settle and both replacement sweeps with manual list/revoke by replacementName and the late-after-final-sweep risk, hand-created token recovery for gone items, overlap expiry, no-running recovery, standalone exclusions and manual equivalents. Replace manual rotation bullets and update pinned-release text; explain measured W and the doubled-runs bound only for I >= 200 ms, its separate non-gating floor(W/max(I,R))+1 estimate below 200 ms, and the different surplus-E bound only for I > 700 ms (Performance impact 2). All unit fault matrices belong here; real overlap/continuity/resume checks belong to T6.

tasks.title: pulse upgrade verifies digests and restores both images and data after failure
tasks.spec: ## Repository: deploy, registry, provenance, snapshot, upgrade, command wiring and docs; Decisions 1, 3 and 10-13; Required behavior (upgrade and Help and docs); Counterexamples (Upgrade versions, Image shapes, Compose edit, Data mounts, Provenance, Snapshot boundary, Rollback); Acceptance evidence 2 (production behavior), 3 (Data mounts, upgrade and state-write matrices), 5-6; Performance impact 3 and Security impact (upgrade). Reuse cli/services.ts's exported assertPin/PULSE_IMAGE, cli/docker.ts's own()/spawn/project guard/text safety, cli/lock.ts, cli/safe-write.ts's single state/file seam, cli/ready.ts and the sole fake spawn. Keep the snapshot/apply/rollback algorithm and its recovery matrices together. Implement injected fixed-host ghcr.io fetch with numeric stable SemVer, <=10 pages, redirect:error, 20 s requests, 1 MiB cap and checked index media type/digest. Validate --to (optional v, no leading zeros/prereleases), installed raw Compose pins, consistent probes and effective-image overrides; refuse dev/downgrades/missing tags. In snapshot.ts validate persistent mounts from Project's effective model (the SAME guarded config call, including overrides) BEFORE any gh/provenance spawn, pull or stop, in preview and apply. Inspect all pulse-kind services: each mount must be a named volume with source in top-level volumes, or a read-only bind; refuse writable binds, tmpfs, anonymous/unknown types. Snapshot every writable volume source regardless of key suffix, sorted and deduplicated; omit unmounted declarations and read-only volumes. Require api, notify and console, when present, each to have exactly one writable named volume at /data, and their PULSE_DB/PULSE_NOTIFY_STATE/PULSE_CONSOLE_DB variable absent or literally equal to the image default. Refuse moved paths and uninterpolated ${...}. Guard-validated names are <project>_<key>. Use Decision 10's fixed refusal texts and recovery link. Record this exact snapshotVolumes set in upgrade.json and require tars keys to equal it when validating complete states. Mount fixture tests belong here with the code. Require installed authenticated gh and verify every changed digest within 120 s using repo, signer-workflow, source-ref and deny-self-hosted-runners even in preview, with no bypass. Verify/pull/write the same digest without resolving it again. Preview has 0 writes/mutations; apply shares the lock and refuses a rotation journal and incomplete/unreadable snapshots, including restored and rollback-failed. Pull before stop. In snapshot.ts validate upgrade.json and own its states snapshotting/applying/done/aborted/rolling-back/restored/rolled-back/rollback-failed (restored:true|false). Stream every key of the effective snapshotVolumes set, in sorted order, to wx 0600 .tar.part fds under a unique 0700 directory using the named, pinned secrets-init helper and Decision 13 restrictions; fsync, size/hash, rename, directory fsync each tar; copy/fsync/hash Compose. The snapshot-complete boundary is the on-disk applying with all tars: either a durable write or read-back after a failed write. Only a durable applying permits the image switch; read-back applying after a failed write rolls back. Resolve EVERY state-write failure by ONE validated disk read-back and the Decision 13 State-write errors table; never infer the state from an exception, retry the write or delete archives referenced by applying. Failed snapshotting write: stop nothing, remove newly created directory/files or leave blocking recovery directory if cleanup fails. Failed applying before rename reads snapshotting -> abort; rename landed/directory-fsync failed reads applying+tars -> full rollback, retain all archives. Applying unreadable/invalid/unexpected -> no deletion/restore/start, exit 1/recovery link. Abort is entered only from on-disk snapshotting: remove/wait for named helper, verify unchanged Compose hash, write aborted, delete archives ONLY after durable aborted then fsync, start unchanged old images/readiness. Failed aborted write keeps every archive, prints snapshot directory kept, starts old images, exits 1; changed Compose refuses with no start/deletion/restore. After the boundary, write rolling-back durably, stop, verify ALL tars and Compose before ANY volume change, restore every volume then Compose, durably write restored BEFORE up/readiness. A failed rolling-back/restored write stops the stack, restores/starts nothing further and retains recovery metadata/archives; no old start while metadata says rolling-back. Corrupt tar or restore failure -> rollback-failed/restored:false, no start. Ready rollback -> rolled-back; old readiness failure after restored -> rollback-failed/restored:true. Failed done/rolled-back/rollback-failed write leaves final stack shape intact and exits 1 with state-file warning, never a fresh rollback. Edit only image strings with replacement-count/model checks and preserve Compose mode. Omit rendered read-only *-secrets mounts from the snapshot set; do not select data by a key suffix or include unused declarations. Data volumes are never deleted outside the restore. Implement success/abort/rollback messages and 0/1/130 outcomes, timeout default 300 s in 1-3600, recorded signals during state-error resolution/rollback, snapshot bytes/time and downtime. Wire HELP/COMMANDS/dispatch/errors and docs with manual equivalents. Document Decision 10's supported data layout, the three default data paths, preflight refusal and how to move a bind-mounted store back into a named volume before upgrading. Upgrade recovery follows facts on disk per Decision 13: snapshotting/unreadable, aborted, applying (Compose byte-equal, to-refs+ready, or restore), rolling-back, restored and rollback-failed true/false, with tar verification before restore. State truthful-before-start, no auto-resume, downtime, lost writes and disk space are documented. Unit matrices stay here; real release fixtures/provenance/migration jobs belong to T6.

acceptance.expected: 0 failing tests; literal tag fixture selects 0.10.0, ignores 0.2.0-rc.1 and accepts optional v for exact stable --to. tasks.spec: ## Repository: deploy, live scripts, CI, Checks and Completion evidence; Acceptance evidence 1-6; Decision 15; Counterexamples (Gap rule, Extra samples, Release fixtures of the live test); all Security impact, Performance impact, Risks and Rollout order. FIRST put shared sample statistics and Docker-event parsing in cli/test/samples.sh with literal-fixture samples.test.sh, then source it in rotate.sh and upgrade.sh; do not duplicate statistics/test setup. Require fully paginated per-location history through before the window start; gap uses window edges and <=5500 ms. E=N-C uses only samples, including first/last, with the greedy latest-reachable chain at <=5500 ms; compute E only after gap passes and N>=2. Test every Extra samples fixture, lemma prerequisites and bound, including phase offset and nearly-in-phase cases. Provide doubled_runs_bound I W only for I>=200 (floor(W/(I-100))+1); lower I exits 2 with no bound below 200 ms. Provide extra_samples_bound I W only for I>700 (2*floor(W/(I-100))+3); otherwise exit 2. Test the literal outputs and refusal cases from Counterexamples; never divide by zero or return a negative bound. Use these shared functions in rotate.sh rather than a second formula, and report K beside the doubled-runs bound. Record docker events independently around ordinary and interrupted rotations: match service labels and full old/new IDs, convert start/die timeNano to T_s/T_d, W=T_d-T_s. Do not infer W from CLI output or the fixed 2000 ms wait. rotate.sh gates baseline E=0, 0<W<=20000, exactly 1 new start/1 old die per ordinary handoff, E<=2*floor(W/4900)+3 over the rotation window with >=2 samples before T_s and >=2 at/after T_d, and E=0 with >=5 samples after T_d. Use the real pinned CLI demo, 60 s baseline, full probe/admin rotation, unaffected IDs/StartedAt, one final probe container, real overlap retry/expiry, secrecy and down/up persistence. After overlap interrupt eu handoff with recorded newContainerId, require exit 130/journal, no-flags resume without another rotate (API rotatedAt unchanged), retain that new container, no journal, eu continuity and E=0 after event-derived T_d. Report per-location gap/E/bound and Docker-event W next to CLI inspect-derived W, sampled probe memory/CPU each second versus baseline. upgrade.sh independently selects the TWO LOWEST stable registry tags A/B common to all five images with curl/jq HEAD digests and no version/digest literals in scripts; test release selection Counterexamples using runtime-assembled non-pin fixtures. Enforce A schema 3/self 404, B schema 9/self 200 regardless of pins. pin-release.sh sets A only in the test install. Test legacy refusal and no-mutation preview. Before B is pulled locally, add the Acceptance 2 writable api-/data bind override over an otherwise valid A stack; BOTH preview and --yes must exit 1 with pulse upgrade can snapshot only named volumes, unchanged Compose hash/container IDs/StartedAt, no locally present B digests and no .pulse-upgrade directory. Remove the override without applying it and continue; test-only pass-through Docker shim holds tar 20 s for SIGINT during .tar.part (abort without restore), then breaks B console readiness to prove migration to 9 followed by restore to schema 3, then real B reaches ready and rotates. Production has no bypass. Report snapshot bytes/time, du -sb, downtime and independent largest result gap using shared samples.sh without the rotation bound. Add cli-rotate/cli-upgrade with 40 min timeouts, existing action SHA pins/Bun 1.4.0, persist-credentials:false, gh --version first, read-only upgrade job token permissions, sample self-test, failure ps --all and always pulse down --volumes teardown. Explicitly shellcheck/bash-n the extensionless shim. Complete README/AGENTS commands/CI and all command/recovery docs and known limits, including in-process reconciliation after every stage error, cleanup-fsync failure recovery, and the owned-file rule with the sole independent admin-bearer exception for probe confirmation. Extra request load differs from surplus E: document floor(W/(I-e))+1 ONLY for I>=200 ms (W=6000: I=5000 -> 2, I=1000 -> 7, I=200 -> 61). Below 200 ms document the separate NON-GATING estimate floor(W/max(I,R))+1, with R measured and api latencyMs its lower bound; at I=1 ms and R=2-10 ms the spec estimates about 600-3000 doubled runs. Recommend avoiding short-interval rotation at busy times. Document that extra_samples_bound has the stricter I>700 lemma domain; the demo's literal I=5000 satisfies both. Run whole-change checks, security checklist and exact Completion evidence from actual green job logs/PR body, including Breaking: no. Follow Risks holds if Compose handoff or release config migrations break acceptance; do not relax gates or add migrations. Include the unified first-run/resume Rotate outcome decisions and literal read-order event log in security/evidence checks. Assert BOTH permitted replacement-entry cases (changed rotatedAt readback, or parsed ok answer lost after stage-error reconcile found no staging file), never a transport error alone. Verify API_SCRIPT's marker/self-exit, settle-before-sweep/create ordering across runs, the 500 ms/30 s limit, at most 2 creates per item/run, final exact-name sweep in switched before lost-token revoke/journal deletion, and no revoke of a held/calling token. Docs must name the late-create-after-final-sweep risk with manual list/revoke by replacementName. Review the effective persistent-mount validation before provenance/pull/stop in preview/apply and snapshotVolumes coverage independent of volume suffix; include supported-layout refusal in PR evidence and docs. Verify the snapshot state-read-back table, durable-aborted-before-deletion rule, restored-before-old-start rule and truthful hard-kill manual recovery, including applying rename success followed by directory-fsync failure.
